title: Conflict Theory and the Palestine Problem

raw_affiliation_strings: Johan Galtung is editor of the Journal of Peace Research at the International Peace Research Institute, Oslo. A longer version of this article has appeared in the Journal of Peace Research

The basis of this article is the search for a language in which the conflict can be formulated. Such a language of conflict would permit the formulation of solutions that cannot be arrived at easily in ordinary discourse. For that reason the conflict language should broaden the concept of reality, expanding it by bringing in possibilities that belong to potential rather than empirical reality. But an adequately formulated solution is neither a sufficient nor a necessary condition for a real life solution which will have to be in the hands of the participants themselves

This study is based more on theory than on data. The author claims no expertise in "Middle East affairs," as this web of human tragedy is sometimes euphemistically referred to. A study tour to Israel in 1966 and several trips to Arab states (Egypt in 1961, 1966, 1969, Gaza in 1964, Syria-Jordan-Iraq in 1969, to Egypt again in 1971 as Visiting Professor at Cairo University with side-trips to Kuwait, Lebanon, Syria and Jordan) provided much important material and above all invaluable discussions. But this article is based on a strong feeling that the basic facts are few and well known, as are the basic principles for evaluating them, and that the rest is a question of ceaseless efforts of search and research for a possible future. I am deeply indebted to friends and colleagues on either side, well aware that many of them would disagree with much, even most of what I say
